module.title: Unit 3: Interpreting Academic Research Data & Charts
module.objective: Mampu menganalisis data survei, grafik batang, dan tren demografis dengan bahasa deskriptif akademis presisi.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Making Sense of Survey Data
subModules.grammarFocus: Reporting findings, describing changes, and using cautious language
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Survey results, demographic groups, proportions, and trends

content.summary: In this module, you will read a short report about a survey on commuting habits. You will practise finding the main message, checking figures in a chart, and describing trends without making claims that the data cannot support. You will also notice useful language for reporting research findings.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use reporting verbs with that-clauses, phrases such as 'There was a steady increase in', and cautious expressions such as 'The findings suggest that'.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn words for population groups, relationships between variables, proportions, and changes in data.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the title and first sentence of each paragraph for the main idea. Then scan for figures, dates, categories, and words that describe changes.

learningObjectives: Identify the main finding in a short report about commuting habits.
Locate figures and compare categories in a bar chart and a line chart.
Recognise words that describe proportions, relationships, and changes in data.
Distinguish a reported correlation from a claim about cause and effect.
Use reporting and cautious language to describe research results accurately.

contextWarmup.prompt: A university asks students how they travel to campus. Which detail would help readers understand who took part in the survey?
options: The age groups and number of students surveyed
The colour used for the chart title
The name of the person who printed the report
contextWarmup.explanation: The age groups and sample size describe the survey's participants. These details help readers judge which population the results may represent.

rules: Use 'showed', 'revealed', or 'indicated' with a that-clause to report a finding: 'The survey revealed that bus use was highest among first-year students.'
Use 'There was a' plus an adjective and a change noun to describe a trend: 'There was a slight fall in cycling from May to June.'
Use 'The data suggests that' or 'The findings suggest that' when an interpretation is possible but not certain.
A correlation means that two variables are related in the data. It does not prove that one variable caused the other.
Check the chart title, units, dates, and categories before comparing figures.

commonTrap.explanation: A link between two variables does not automatically show that one caused the other. Survey results may reveal a correlation, but other factors could also explain the pattern.
commonTrap.wrong: The survey found that students who cycled felt healthier, so cycling caused their better health.
commonTrap.correct: The survey found a correlation between cycling and reported health. The results do not prove that cycling caused the difference.

content.passageTitle: How Students Travel to Northbridge College
paragraphs: Northbridge College surveyed 600 students in March to find out how they travelled to campus. The sample included first-year and final-year students from several age groups. Respondents selected one main travel method. The report presents the results as percentages, so the figures describe the share of answers rather than the number of journeys made each day.

The bar chart shows that buses were the most common choice overall, accounting for 38% of responses. Walking accounted for 26%, while 20% of students travelled by bicycle. Trains and cars made up the remaining 16%. A larger proportion of first-year students walked than final-year students, but the report does not give enough detail to explain why.

A second chart tracks cycling between January and June. The proportion of students cycling rose from 14% in January to 19% in March, then reached 24% in May. In June, it fell slightly to 23%. This suggests a general rise over the period, although the monthly figures did not increase every time. The level may have begun to plateau near the end of the study.

The researchers also found a correlation between living close to campus and choosing to walk. This relationship does not show that living nearby caused students to walk, since factors such as timetable and transport costs may matter too. The findings suggest that distance is relevant, but the survey cannot establish a single cause. A follow-up study could ask students why they choose each travel method.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the Northbridge College survey?
options: To find out how students travelled to campus
To compare students' exam results
To measure the cost of public transport
questions.answer: To find out how students travelled to campus
questions.explanation: The first sentence says the survey aimed to find out how students travelled to campus.

questions.question: How many students took part in the survey?
questions.explanation: The report states that Northbridge College surveyed 600 students.

questions.question: What does the report's use of percentages describe?
options: The share of answers for each travel method
The number of journeys each student made every day
The distance each student travelled
questions.answer: The share of answers for each travel method
questions.explanation: The first paragraph explains that the percentages show the share of answers, not daily journey counts.

questions.question: Which travel method was the most common overall?
options: Walking
Bus
Bicycle
questions.explanation: Buses accounted for 38% of responses, the highest share in the bar chart.

questions.question: What percentage of students travelled by bicycle in the overall survey?
questions.explanation: The report says that 20% of students travelled by bicycle.

questions.question: How did the proportion of students cycling change between January and May?
options: It rose from 14% to 24%.
It fell from 24% to 14%.
It stayed at 19%.
questions.explanation: The second chart shows 14% in January and 24% in May.

questions.question: What happened to cycling in June?
options: It rose to 29%.
It fell slightly to 23%.
It returned to 14%.
questions.explanation: The report says the figure fell slightly from 24% in May to 23% in June.

questions.question: What does the report say the correlation between living near campus and walking proves?
options: Living nearby causes every student to walk.
It does not prove that living nearby caused students to walk.
Students who live far away never walk.
questions.answer: It does not prove that living nearby caused students to walk.
questions.explanation: The report warns that a correlation does not establish cause and effect, and other factors may matter.

questions.question: Why does the report use the phrase 'The findings suggest'?
options: To present a careful interpretation rather than an absolute claim
To show that all participants gave the same answer
To introduce a figure that was not measured
questions.answer: To present a careful interpretation rather than an absolute claim
questions.explanation: The wording signals that distance may be relevant, while acknowledging that the survey cannot establish one cause.

questions.question: What could a follow-up study ask students?
options: Why they choose each travel method
Which chart colour they prefer
How many classes they attend each week
questions.answer: Why they choose each travel method
questions.explanation: The final sentence proposes asking students why they choose each way of travelling.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Interpreting Academic Survey Trends

content.summary: Learn how to follow academic discussions where speakers evaluate bar charts, compare percentages, and interpret demographic patterns. Pay attention to how speakers hedge conclusions and link words when reading data aloud.
learningObjectives: Catch precise numerical changes and trends in spoken discussions
Identify demographic categories and comparative statements quickly
Notice consonant-to-vowel linking in rapid academic speech

keyPhrases.note: Commonly used in academic reports to describe a proportion or percentage.
Refers to sorting data into groups such as age, gender, or income.
Used to show that two data sources or observations support each other.
A cautious hedging phrase used when evidence is incomplete.

connectedSpeech.note: The final /k/ in 'look' links directly into the vowel in 'at'.
The unvoiced /t/ ending connects straight into the diphthong /eɪ/.
The /k/ of 'check' merges cleanly into the vowel sound /aʊ/.
The consonant cluster /dʒd/ links to 'at', and the final /t/ connects into 'all'.

content.summary: Use precise language to report survey findings, describe changes in charts, and interpret trends cautiously. Support each claim with figures where possible, and avoid presenting a possible explanation as a proven fact.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Report a Finding
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + showed / revealed / indicated + that + clause
blueprintItems.example: The survey results revealed that 68% of respondents preferred online learning.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Describe a Change
blueprintItems.formula: There was a + adjective + noun + in + noun + from X to Y
blueprintItems.example: There was a steady increase in participation from 42% to 57%.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Interpret with Caution
blueprintItems.formula: The data suggests / The findings suggest + that + clause
blueprintItems.example: The findings suggest that younger adults use the service more frequently.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the past tense to report a completed survey or study.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The survey shows that 62% chose option A last year.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The survey showed that 62% chose option A last year.
mechanicsRules.why: The survey took place in the past, so the reporting verb should normally be in the past tense.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction when it joins two independent clauses.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The rate rose in 2020 but it fell the following year.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The rate rose in 2020, but it fell the following year.
mechanicsRules.why: Both parts can stand as complete sentences, so a comma is used before but.

mechanicsRules.rule: Include a space between a number and a percentage symbol only when the required style guide specifies it; use one format consistently.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The figure increased from 18% to 24 percent.
mechanicsRules.why: Consistent formatting makes numerical comparisons easier to read.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Summarise a Survey
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write a short paragraph of four to five sentences about these results: 60% of participants used a mobile app, 25% used a website, and 15% visited an office. Report the figures accurately and include one cautious interpretation.
guidedLabChallenges.example: The survey showed that 60% of participants used a mobile app. A quarter used a website, while 15% visited an office. The findings suggest that digital services were more popular among this group.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Describe a Demographic Trend
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write four to five sentences describing this chart: the proportion of residents aged 18 to 29 who cycled to work rose from 12% in 2019 to 20% in 2022, while the figure for residents aged 50 to 64 stayed at about 8%. Compare the groups and avoid making unsupported claims about the cause.
guidedLabChallenges.example: The chart showed that cycling to work became more common among residents aged 18 to 29. Their proportion rose from 12% in 2019 to 20% in 2022. By contrast, the figure for those aged 50 to 64 remained at around 8%. The data suggests that cycling rates changed differently across the two age groups.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Describe and compare the trends here...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using the reporting verb indicated.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The data showed that 72% of respondents supported the proposal. Use revealed.
practicumQuestions.hint: Keep the tense and the rest of the finding unchanged.
targetAnswers: The data revealed that 72% of respondents supported the proposal.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Revealed can replace showed to report a finding. Keep the past tense because the data refers to a completed study.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the information using the change pattern in the hint.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The rate rose from 8% in 2019 to 14% in 2022. Describe it as a significant increase.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with There was a significant increase.
targetAnswers: There was a significant increase in the rate from 8% in 2019 to 14% in 2022.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The pattern There was a significant increase in describes a change and gives its starting and ending values.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the claim using cautious academic language.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Younger adults use the service more often. Begin with The findings suggest.
targetAnswers: The findings suggest that younger adults use the service more often.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Suggest makes the interpretation cautious rather than presenting it as certain.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the sentences with although to show contrast.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The total number of users increased. The proportion of older users remained stable.
practicumQuestions.hint: Put although before the contrasting clause.
targetAnswers: Although the total number of users increased, the proportion of older users remained stable.
The proportion of older users remained stable although the total number of users increased.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Although introduces information that contrasts with the main point. Use a comma when the although clause comes first.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with a suitable conjunction.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The figure rose from 15% to 21%, ___ the increase was smaller among rural residents.
practicumQuestions.hint: Choose a conjunction that shows contrast.
targetAnswers: The figure rose from 15% to 21%, but the increase was smaller among rural residents.
The figure rose from 15% to 21%, whereas the increase was smaller among rural residents.
practicumQuestions.explanation: But and whereas can both introduce a contrasting point. The comma separates the two clauses.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the capitalization, verb tense, and punctuation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: the survey show that 48% of adults use the service last year
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the opening word and use past tense for the survey and its result.
targetAnswers: The survey showed that 48% of adults used the service last year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Capitalize the first word, use showed and used for a completed survey, and end the sentence with a full stop.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the grammar and punctuation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: There was a steady increase in participation from 31% at 2020 to 45% at 2023
practicumQuestions.hint: Use in with years and add the final punctuation.
targetAnswers: There was a steady increase in participation from 31% in 2020 to 45% in 2023.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use in before years and add a full stop to complete the sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the subject-verb agreement and punctuation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The findings suggests that income influence technology use
practicumQuestions.hint: Find the subject of each verb.
targetAnswers: The findings suggest that income influences technology use.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Findings is plural, so it takes suggest. Income is singular, so it takes influences.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write one sentence reporting both figures from the prompt.
practicumQuestions.promptText: In a survey, 63% of first-year students studied online, compared with 41% of final-year students.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use revealed that and include both percentages.
targetAnswers: The survey revealed that 63% of first-year students studied online, compared with 41% of final-year students.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A clear response reports both groups and their figures without changing the meaning of the comparison.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write two sentences describing the trend and offering a cautious interpretation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The share of households using solar energy rose from 10% in 2020 to 18% in 2023.
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe the increase first, then begin your interpretation with The data suggests.
targetAnswers: There was a significant increase in the share of households using solar energy from 10% in 2020 to 18% in 2023. The data suggests that interest in solar energy may be growing.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The first sentence reports the measured change. The second offers a cautious interpretation and avoids claiming a proven cause.

content.summary: Explain what a chart shows before interpreting it. Identify the population, variables, units, and time period. Use precise language to describe proportions, changes, and comparisons. Distinguish correlation from causation: two variables can be related without one causing the other.
content.audioGuidance: Say percentages and figures clearly, and pause briefly between the overview and supporting details. Stress the key information in comparisons, such as higher, lower, and account for. Use falling intonation when completing a statement, and rising intonation when checking a detail or inviting a response.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Keep vowel sounds distinct in words such as data, mean, and trend. Avoid shortening a long vowel when saying a figure or a key term.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.explanation: Place the main stress clearly in words such as demographic and correlation. Practise the stressed syllable without making every syllable equally strong.

pillars.name: Chart Language
pillars.target: Precise descriptions of change and proportion
pillars.explanation: Use verbs such as rise, fall, fluctuate, and plateau to describe movement. Use account for to state what share of a total a category represents.

pillars.name: Careful Interpretation
pillars.explanation: Support interpretations with figures from the chart. Use cautious phrases such as the data suggest and appears to be associated with when the evidence does not prove causation.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The main stress remains on GRAPH when the plural ending is added.
Keep the main stress on LA in both the singular and plural forms.
The main stress stays on POR when you add the plural ending.
The stress changes from the final syllable in fluctuate to the third syllable in fluctuation.

drills.targetText: The data show a correlation between exercise and reported well-being.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˈdeɪtə ʃəʊ ə ˌkɒrəˈleɪʃən bɪˈtwiːn ˈeksəsaɪz ænd rɪˈpɔːtɪd ˌwelˈbiːɪŋ/
drills.focus: Stress in correlation and clear delivery of a research finding
drills.hint: Stress LAY in correlation. Pause briefly before the phrase between exercise and reported well-being.

drills.targetText: The proportion of participants reporting stress fluctuated during the first three months.
drills.phonetic: /ðə prəˈpɔːʃən əv pɑːˈtɪsɪpənts rɪˈpɔːtɪŋ stres ˈflʌktʃueɪtɪd ˈdjʊərɪŋ ðə fɜːst θriː mʌnθs/
drills.focus: Syllable stress and the consonant cluster in fluctuated
drills.hint: Stress POR in proportion and ATE in fluctuated. Say the ending of fluctuated clearly.

drills.targetText: The increase levelled off, and the figure then plateaued at around sixty per cent.
drills.phonetic: /ði ˈɪŋkriːs ˌlevəld ˈɒf ænd ðə ˈfɪɡə ðen plæˈtəʊd ət əˈraʊnd ˈsɪksti pə ˈsent/
drills.focus: Falling intonation and clear pronunciation of plateaued
drills.hint: Use a calm falling tone at the end of the statement. Make the final syllable of plateaued clear.

roleplay.context: You are discussing a bar chart with a research partner before a class presentation. The chart compares reported weekly exercise across three age groups and shows that the figures rise overall, with a small decline in the oldest group.

turns.speaker: Research Partner
turns.text: What is the main pattern in the bar chart?
turns.translation: Apa pola utama dalam diagram batang tersebut?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Weekly exercise rises across the first two age groups, then falls slightly in the oldest group.
turns.translation: Olahraga mingguan meningkat pada dua kelompok usia pertama, lalu sedikit menurun pada kelompok usia tertua.

turns.speaker: Research Partner
turns.text: Which group accounts for the largest proportion of reported exercise?
turns.translation: Kelompok mana yang menyumbang proporsi terbesar dari olahraga yang dilaporkan?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: The middle age group has the highest figure, although the difference from the youngest group is small.
turns.translation: Kelompok usia menengah memiliki angka tertinggi, meskipun selisihnya dengan kelompok termuda kecil.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Describe the chart in a clear order, from its overall pattern to one or two supporting figures.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Imagine a bar chart comparing weekly screen time among three age groups. Describe what it shows and point out the most important comparison.
storyPoints: Name the age groups and explain what the bars measure.
Describe which group has the highest and lowest screen time, using approximate figures.
Summarise the main comparison and mention one limitation of the data.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The oldest group reports the highest weekly screen time, while the youngest group records the lowest figure.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ˈəʊldɪst ɡruːp rɪˈpɔːts ðə ˈhaɪɪst ˈwiːkli skriːn taɪm waɪl ðə ˈjʌŋɡɪst ɡruːp rɪˈkɔːdz ðə ˈləʊɪst ˈfɪɡə/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Organise the description logically, use comparative language, and support your interpretation with figures rather than unsupported claims.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a survey result. Use cautious language when interpreting the relationship between variables.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A survey found that people who exercised more often also reported higher well-being. Explain the result without claiming that exercise definitely caused the difference.
storyPoints: Identify the two variables and the group surveyed.
Describe the direction of the reported correlation.
Explain why correlation alone does not prove cause and effect.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The survey found a positive correlation between exercise frequency and reported well-being, but it cannot establish causation.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈsɜːveɪ faʊnd ə ˈpɒzətɪv ˌkɒrəˈleɪʃən bɪˈtwiːn ˈeksəsaɪz ˈfriːkwənsi ænd rɪˈpɔːtɪd ˌwelˈbiːɪŋ bət ɪt ˈkænɒt ɪˈstæblɪʃ kɔːˈzeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use accurate statistical language and make clear that an association between variables does not show that one variable caused the other.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond as a student presenting survey results to a seminar group. Give a short overview, then support it with an accurate detail.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your tutor asks what the survey was designed to measure. Explain its focus and identify the population.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are presenting a survey on commuting habits to your seminar group. The survey focuses on university students aged 18 to 25.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the student presenter. Explain the survey aim and define the demographic clearly.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The survey examines commuting habits among the 18-to-25 demographic at the university.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈsɜːveɪ ɪɡˈzæmɪnz kəˈmjuːtɪŋ ˈhæbɪts əˈmʌŋ ði ˌeɪˈtiːn tə ˌtwenti ˈfaɪv ˌdeməˈɡræfɪk ət ðə ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːsəti/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Define the population precisely and use present simple to describe the survey's purpose.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to a partner asking you to describe a trend. Mention the direction of change and where it stabilises.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your research partner asks what happened to the participation rate over the period shown in a line graph.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You and a research partner are preparing a presentation about participation in an online learning programme. The line graph shows a rapid rise followed by a stable period.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the student responsible for describing the graph. Explain the rise and the later plateau.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Participation rose sharply at first, then plateaued at around 60 percent.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /pɑːˌtɪsɪˈpeɪʃən rəʊz ˈʃɑːpli ət fɜːst ðen plæˈtəʊd ət əˈraʊnd ˈsɪksti pə ˈsent/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use past simple for a completed period and choose a verb that accurately describes the stable section.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Answer a question about how categories contribute to a total. Use account for and state the proportion clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A colleague asks how much of the total was represented by public transport users.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are discussing a pie chart of commuting methods with a colleague. Public transport represents 35 percent of the responses.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the student explaining the chart. State the share represented by public transport users.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Public transport accounted for 35 percent of the responses.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈpʌblɪk ˈtrænspɔːt əˈkaʊntɪd fə ˌθɜːti ˈfaɪv pə ˈsent əv ðə rɪˈspɒnsɪz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use account for to describe a category's share of the total, and pronounce the percentage clearly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to a tutor who challenges your conclusion. Explain what the data can show and what it cannot prove.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your tutor asks whether a correlation in your results proves that one factor caused another. Give a careful response.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: In a class discussion, you have described a correlation between time spent studying and exam scores. Your tutor asks you to interpret the finding cautiously.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the student researcher. Acknowledge the association but avoid claiming that it proves causation.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The variables are associated in this sample, but the result does not prove that study time caused higher scores.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈveəriəbəlz ə əˈsəʊsieɪtɪd ɪn ðɪs ˈsɑːmpəl bət ðə rɪˈzʌlt dʌz nɒt pruːv ðət ˈstʌdi taɪm kɔːzd ˈhaɪə skɔːz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Show appropriate caution by distinguishing an observed association from a proven cause-and-effect relationship.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Use demographic, proportion, fluctuate, and plateau in four short spoken sentences about research data.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a population group, a share of the total, an irregular change, and a figure that later becomes stable.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The proportion for this demographic fluctuated before it plateaued.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə prəˈpɔːʃən fə ðɪs ˌdeməˈɡræfɪk ˈflʌktʃueɪtɪd bɪˈfɔː ɪt plæˈtəʊd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use each word with its correct meaning and grammatical form. Give a clear, relevant example for each term.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Describe a completed change in a graph using the past simple, then report a percentage using account for.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say that renewable energy represented 29 percent of electricity generation in 2023, then describe how its share changed that year.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Renewable energy accounted for 29 percent of electricity generation in 2023, and its share rose slightly.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /rɪˈnjuːəbəl ˈenədʒi əˈkaʊntɪd fə ˌtwenti ˈnaɪn pə ˈsent əv ɪˌlekˈtrɪsəti ˌdʒenəˈreɪʃən ɪn ˌtwenti ˌtwenti ˈθriː ænd ɪts ʃeə rəʊz ˈslaɪtli/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use past forms for a completed time period and place the percentage immediately after accounted for.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say demographic, correlation, and proportion twice. Make the stressed syllable noticeably stronger without stressing every syllable.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen for the main stress: demoGRAPHic, correLAtion, proPORtion.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The demographic showed a correlation in the proportion of responses.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˌdeməˈɡræfɪk ʃəʊd ə ˌkɒrəˈleɪʃən ɪn ðə prəˈpɔːʃən əv rɪˈspɒnsɪz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Place the main stress on GRAPH in demographic, LAY in correlation, and POR in proportion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the first sentence with falling intonation. Read the follow-up question with rising intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise the contrast: The percentage rose to 40 percent. Did it then plateau?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The percentage rose to 40 percent. Did it then plateau?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə pəˈsentɪdʒ rəʊz tə ˈfɔːti pə ˈsent | dɪd ɪt ðen plæˈtəʊ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice fall at the end of the completed statement. Let it rise slightly at the end of the yes-or-no question.
